newsitem.title: USA: Key U.S. senator opposes SPR oil sale.
newsitem.headline: Key U.S. senator opposes SPR oil sale.

text.p: The chairman of the Senate Energy Committee has urged lawmakers not to approve a sale of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve as a budget saving measure, Senate staff said Thursday.

Sen. Frank Murkowski, an Alaska Republican, told lawmakers that the oil sale was costing, not saving, taxpayers' money in the long run and that the emergency stockpile should be left intact, the staff said.

"I would like to reiterate my opposition to sales of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve for purposes of offsetting appropriations," he said in a letter directed to senators involved in the interior and energy spending bill that was obtained by Reuters.

In the letter, he said three oil sales in the last two years designed to close the U.S. budget gap had cost taxpayers almost $500 million, because oil in the reserve had cost $33 per barrel to buy and store, while the average sale price had been $17.77 per barrel.

"Buying high and selling low never makes sense," he said, echoing complaints by House lawmakers who opposed a $209 million oil sale included in the House's fiscal year 1998 interior spending bill to cover the costs of running the SPR.
"The value of the oil in the SPR today is minuscule compared to value that it will have in future energy crises," Murkowski said.
